title: 50 Most Asked API Interview Questions
summary: The 50 API questions backend/SDE interviewers ask most, grouped into themed pages from REST and HTTP basics through auth, security, pagination, rate limiting, caching, gateways, webhooks, idempotency, versioning, testing, monitoring, scalability and real-world design scenarios. Each answer gives a short direct reply, key points and a visual.

chapters.title: 50 API Interview Questions: What's Inside
points: REST and HTTP basics
Methods and status codes
JWT and sessions
OAuth 2.0 and API keys
CORS and API security
Pagination and filtering
Rate limiting and caching
API gateway and webhooks
Idempotency, versioning and file uploads
Testing and monitoring
Scalability and performance
Real-world API design scenarios

chapters.title: REST and HTTP Basics
points: What is a REST API and what are its constraints?
What is the difference between REST and SOAP?
What is the difference between REST, GraphQL and gRPC?
What does stateless mean in REST and why does it matter?
What are the parts of an HTTP request and response?

chapters.title: Methods and Status Codes
points: What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?
What is the difference between safe and idempotent HTTP methods?
What is the difference between 401 and 403?
When do you return 400, 404, 409, 422 and 429?

chapters.title: JWT and Sessions
points: What is a JWT and how is it structured?
What is the difference between session-based and token-based authentication?
How do access tokens and refresh tokens work together?
How do you revoke or invalidate a JWT before it expires?

chapters.title: OAuth 2.0 and API Keys
points: How does the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow work?
What is the difference between OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect?
Why is PKCE needed and which OAuth grant types exist?
What is the difference between API keys, Basic auth and Bearer tokens?

chapters.title: CORS and API Security
points: What is CORS and how does a preflight request work?
What is the difference between CORS and CSRF?
What are BOLA/IDOR vulnerabilities and how do you prevent them?
How do you prevent SQL injection and mass assignment in an API?
How do you secure an API in production (HTTPS, headers, validation, secrets)?

chapters.title: Pagination and Filtering
points: What is the difference between offset and cursor pagination?
How does keyset pagination work in SQL?
How do you design filtering, sorting and field selection in a REST API?
How do you return pagination metadata and links (Link header, total count)?

chapters.title: Rate Limiting and Caching
points: How do the token bucket and sliding window rate limiting algorithms work?
How do you implement distributed rate limiting with Redis?
How do ETag and Cache-Control work for HTTP caching?
What are cache-aside, write-through and write-back, and how do you invalidate a cache?

chapters.title: API Gateway and Webhooks
points: What is an API gateway and what does it do?
What is the difference between an API gateway, a reverse proxy and a load balancer?
What is a webhook and how is it different from polling?
How do you secure webhooks and make delivery reliable?

chapters.title: Idempotency, Versioning and File Uploads
points: How do you make a payment POST endpoint idempotent?
What are the API versioning strategies and which would you pick?
How do you handle backward-compatible changes and deprecation?
How do you design large file uploads (multipart, presigned URLs, resumable)?

chapters.title: Testing and Monitoring
points: How do you test an API with unit, integration, contract and load tests?
What is the difference between mocking, stubbing and contract testing?
What are the key metrics to monitor for an API (RED, latency percentiles)?
How do logging, tracing and correlation IDs help debug a production API?

chapters.title: Scalability and Performance
points: How do you scale an API horizontally and why must it be stateless?
How do you reduce the latency of a slow API endpoint?
What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous APIs (202 Accepted and polling)?
How do timeouts, retries with backoff and circuit breakers keep an API resilient?

chapters.title: Real-World API Design Scenarios
points: How would you design a URL shortener API?
How would you design a rate-limited public API for third-party developers?
How would you design the APIs for a checkout and payment flow?
How would you design a real-time notification API (WebSockets vs SSE vs polling)?

chapters.title: API Interview Cheatsheet
points: Safe vs idempotent table: GET, PUT, PATCH, POST, DELETE
Auth picker: session, JWT, OAuth 2.0 + PKCE, API key
Pagination picker: offset vs cursor
Rate limiting algorithms: token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding window
Caching headers: Cache-Control, ETag, If-None-Match, Vary
Resilience checklist: timeout, retry with backoff and jitter, circuit breaker, idempotency key
Answer template for design questions: requirements, endpoints, data model, scale, failure modes
